terms.comment: Traupman’s word, from oscillum, a swing (the lexicon’s playground swing); oscillāris is not in Lewis & Short.

phrases.latin: In sellā oscillārī sedēns avus obdormīvit.
phrases.english: Grandpa fell asleep sitting in the rocking chair.

oscillaris.claim: o left unmarked, its length unsettled
oscillaris.html: Lewis & Short leaves the o unmarked in oscillum and oscillō, and its etymologies differ: from ōs, face, which would make it long, as in ōsculum (so the sources in Festus p. 194 Müll.), or from ob- or obs-cillō. Traupman himself writes oscillum, oscillāre (pp. 53, 389); de Vaan has no entry.

sources: Lewis & Short: sella · Lewis & Short: oscillum · Lewis & Short: oscillo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 53, 372, 389. Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word.
